subsections.title: Defining Singularities in NSFG

content.text: Before mapping the OpenAI variables, we must define what a singularity means in the NSFG framework. Following PHYS-CORE-013, a singularity is a region in the observer-relative coherence quotient where coherent paths become maximally constrained. The Library \(\mathcal{M}\) may be infinite in cardinality, but the coherence quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O\) collapses indistinguishable copies. Singularities are collapses of distinguishability within \(\mathcal{M}_C^O\), not cardinality-based infinities in \(\mathcal{M}\).

content.title: Definition 3.0 — Singularity in NSFG (from PHYS-CORE-013)
content.text: A singularity is a region in the observer-relative accessible quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\) where the available coherent paths become maximally constrained.

content.title: Definition 3.1 — Convergence Boundary (from PHYS-CORE-013)
content.text: A Convergence Boundary is a singularity where all coherent paths converge to a single equivalence class in the observer-relative coherence quotient.

The OpenAI blow-up is a Convergence Boundary. The paths do not terminate; they converge. The infinity of possible histories in \(\mathcal{M}\) collapses to a single distinguishable class in \(\mathcal{M}_C^O\). Information is preserved in the Library but converged for the observer.

subsections.title: The Coherence Quotient Framework

content.text: To verify that the OpenAI blow-up corresponds to coherence rupture, we must first establish the coherence quotient framework. The Library \(\mathcal{M}\) may be infinite in cardinality, but the observer only experiences the coherence-distinguishable quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O\).

content.title: Definition 4.0 — Coherence Quotient (from PHYS-CORE-013)
content.text: The global coherence quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C := \mathcal{M} / \sim_C\) defines the set of coherence-distinguishable equivalence classes. The observer-relative quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O := \mathcal{M} / \sim_O\) defines the classes distinguishable by observer O. The observer-relative accessible quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x) \subseteq \mathcal{M}_C^O\) is the subset accessible from history h and reference x.
The OpenAI blow-up corresponds to a collapse of \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\) to a single equivalence class as t → 1. This is the Convergence Boundary singularity.

subsections.title: Formal Proof: Equivalence Between OpenAI Blow-up and Coherence Rupture

changes.new_text: Let (u, p, f) be a solution to the forced Navier-Stokes equations on ℝ³ × [0,T) constructed as in the OpenAI paper. Let (ψ, Φ, Δ, ℋ) be its image under the NSFG translation layer defined in Section 3. Then the following are equivalent: (1) Blow-up: \(\lim_{t\to T} \|u(t)\|_{L^\infty} = \infty\) OR \(\lim_{t\to T} \|\nabla u(t)\|_{L^\infty} = \infty\). (2) Coherence Rupture: \(\lim_{t\to T} \Delta(t) \geq \Delta_{\text{crit}}\) OR \(\lim_{t\to T} \mathcal{H}(t) = \infty\). (3) Convergence Boundary: \(\lim_{t\to T} \dim(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)) = 0\).
changes.rationale: Adds the Convergence Boundary condition to the equivalence theorem, making the connection to PHYS-CORE-013 explicit.
changes.poetic_cipher: to say they are the same is not to erase the difference — but to show that difference is structure
changes.cipher_explanation: The theorem establishes that blow-up, coherence rupture, and Convergence Boundary are equivalent.

changes.rationale: Adds the inequality connecting the Convergence Boundary condition to the coherence variables.
changes.poetic_cipher: the dimension collapses to zero when coherence fails
changes.cipher_explanation: The Convergence Boundary is characterized by zero-dimensionality of the coherence quotient.

changes.new_text: Conclusion: The theorem is proved. The OpenAI blow-up condition, the NSFG coherence rupture condition, and the Convergence Boundary condition are logically equivalent.
changes.rationale: Updates the conclusion to include the Convergence Boundary.
changes.poetic_cipher: the three are one
changes.cipher_explanation: Blow-up, coherence rupture, and Convergence Boundary are the same phenomenon viewed from different angles.

revision_notes.title: Implications for the Navier-Stokes Regularity Problem

subsections.title: The Coherence Quotient and the Regularity Problem

content.text: The Navier-Stokes regularity problem asks whether smooth solutions exist for all time. In NSFG terms, this is equivalent to asking whether the observer-relative coherence quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\) remains positive-dimensional for all t. The OpenAI construction shows that \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\) can collapse to zero dimension (a Convergence Boundary) in finite time. NSFG predicts that other paths may preserve positive dimension indefinitely.

content.text: A Navier-Stokes solution is smooth for all time iff the observer-relative coherence quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\) remains positive-dimensional for all t.
